# tenzir_configuration_file (Resource)

One text file on one branch of a workspace's configuration repository, such as a pipeline at `pipelines/<name>.tql`. Deployments that follow the branch run what it declares.

Every create, update and delete is one commit, which the provider makes through a draft of the calling user: it starts a draft at the branch tip, saves the change, and commits it. It retries once when the branch moves in between, and discards its draft when it fails. Writes to the same branch wait for each other within one Terraform run.

A user has one draft per branch, which the web UI's editor shares. When that draft holds changes, the provider refuses to write to the branch rather than publish them; an empty draft, as opening the editor starts, is replaced. Run Terraform with an identity that does not edit the branch by hand, and not twice at once.

Creating a file that exists with other content fails; import it instead. Deleting a file that is gone succeeds. Package files (`package.yaml`, `package.lock`, `src/`) are refused, because deployments do not run them yet. After a write, the provider warns when the branch holds something no deployment would take.

Needs a user's credential and `Workspace.read`, `Workspace.readFileTree`, `Workspace.readFile`, `Workspace.readCommit`, `Workspace.readConfiguredPipelines`, `Workspace.createDraft`, `Workspace.readDraft`, `Workspace.saveDraft`, `Workspace.commitDraft` and `Workspace.discardDraft`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tenzir_configuration_file" "ingest" {
  organization_id = data.tenzir_organization.acme.id
  workspace_id    = tenzir_workspace.soc.id
  branch          = "main"
  path            = "pipelines/ingest.tql"
  content         = <<-TQL
    ---
    name: Ingest Suricata alerts
    ---
    from_file "/var/log/suricata/eve.json", follow=true {
      read_suricata
    }
    publish "suricata"
  TQL
  commit_message = "Ingest Suricata alerts"
}

resource "tenzir_configuration_file" "settings" {
  organization_id = data.tenzir_organization.acme.id
  workspace_id    = tenzir_workspace.soc.id
  path            = "tenzir.yaml"
  content         = file("${path.module}/tenzir.yaml")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) The file's text. A pipeline file is TQL, optionally after YAML frontmatter between `---` lines that sets `name` or `disabled`.
- `organization_id` (String) The ID or slug of the organization.
- `path` (String) The file's path in the repository, such as `pipelines/ingest.tql` or `tenzir.yaml`.
- `workspace_id` (String) The ID or slug of the workspace whose repository holds the file.

### Optional

- `branch` (String) The branch that holds the file. Defaults to `main`, which every new workspace has. The branch must exist.
- `commit_message` (String) The message of the commits that create and update the file. Defaults to `terraform: create <path>` or `terraform: update <path>`; deleting says `terraform: delete <path>`. Changing only the message commits nothing.

### Read-Only

- `commit` (String) The commit that holds the content: the one the last write made, or the branch tip when the content was already there. It does not follow later commits to other files.
- `id` (String) `<organization ID>/<workspace ID>/<branch>:<path>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization>/<workspace>/<branch>:<path>, the first two each an ID or a
# slug. The first colon ends the branch, which may contain slashes.
terraform import tenzir_configuration_file.ingest acme/soc/main:pipelines/ingest.tql
```
